observations: Photo 0 shows a green overlock sewing machine with visible wear, including scratches and discoloration on the metal and plastic parts. A red oval sticker with gold text is visible on the side, but the brand name is not legible. The machine is partially wrapped in plastic.

Photo 1 shows the side and back of the same machine, revealing a motor with a white label that is too blurry to read. An orange belt connects the motor to the main shaft. The machine appears to be used, with dust and grime on the surface.

Photo 2 shows a tangled black power cord and a green plastic component (possibly a foot pedal or motor cover) resting on white foam packaging. The cord has a standard Nigerian 3-pin plug. The foam is broken and dirty, suggesting prior use or handling.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show visible wear, scratches, and grime on the machine. Photo 2 shows used foam packaging and a tangled cord, inconsistent with a brand new item.

risks.risk: Machine may not work or have internal damage
risks.proof: Video of the machine running or a close-up of the motor and internal mechanisms showing no rust or damage.

risks.risk: Power cord may be damaged or non-functional
risks.proof: Close-up of the cord's insulation and connectors, and a test video showing it plugged in and powering the machine.
Full inventory shot showing all components included with the machine (e.g., bobbins, needles, manual, foot attachments).

proof_requests: Video of the machine running to confirm functionality.
Close-up of the motor label to identify the brand and model.
Full shot of all included accessories and parts.
Test video of the power cord plugged in and powering the machine.
response.reason: The seller claims the machine is brand new, but the photos show clear signs of use, including wear, grime, and used packaging. Without proof of functionality and completeness, the item cannot be priced accurately. The brand and model are unreadable, and the condition is unverified.
